source.title: SAE-SSV: Supervised Steering in Sparse Representation Spaces for Reliable Control of Language Models
source.authors: Zirui He; Mingyu Jin; Bo Shen; Ali Payani; Yongfeng Zhang; Meng-Nan Du

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies SAE-based representation analysis to LLMs and reports findings about class-discriminative sparse features, an extension to this setting. It does not reproduce the toy-network superposition experiments.
record.gate_note: The representation analyses in Figures 2 and 3 report outcomes relevant to V4. The steering benchmarks, ablations, and examples measure the performance of SAE-SSV, not superposition or feature recovery, so they are not cataloged as claim rows. The paper uses pretrained SAEs to select task-relevant dimensions but does not directly validate recovered features against ground-truth model features.
record.test_reason: This is a steering-method paper. It uses pretrained SAEs (Gemma Scope, Llama Scope) as a tool and reports mainly its own method's performance. The Section 4.3 analyses (Figs 2–3) only motivate the method. They look at supervised, class-discriminative SAE dimensions for sentiment and truthfulness, shown qualitatively. They do not test whether features are superposed, spread across neurons, or recovered by the SAE as the model's own features. So no version of the claim is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that steering constrained to a small, supervised-selected SAE subspace gives higher steering success with less quality loss than CAA, RePe, Top PC and ITI, and that few dimensions suffice. They also note cross-dataset transfer captures stylistic as well as semantic patterns.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses pretrained SAEs and supervised feature selection to build steering vectors; it does not apply the original toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The selected intervention layer varies by model and task. The paper also reports that increasing the inference steering scale generally amplifies semantic shift, with possible quality side effects.

fits_no_version.finding: In LLaMA3.1-8B layer 16, a handful of supervised-selected SAE latents show clearer sentiment and truthfulness class contrast than top raw residual dimensions (qualitative, Fig 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Task attributes are more linearly concentrated in SAE latent space than in the residual basis, which aids steering.

fits_no_version.finding: The top-128 SAE dimensions chosen by the F-statistic and probes are identical across probe ensembles of size 1–50, and a few top dimensions give most of the class separation (Fig 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Supervised SAE dimension selection for a task is stable and concentrated in few latents.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The feature analyses are limited to selected tasks, layers, and models and do not validate SAE features against ground-truth underlying features. The paper notes limited human evaluation and evaluates models only up to 9B parameters. The representation-analysis trends are described without uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: Steering success, quality, generalization, and ablation results in Tables 1, 3, and 4 concern the proposed SAE-SSV method's behavior-control performance rather than the claim's representation geometry or SAE feature recovery. Steering examples and scaling examples are also excluded because they are qualitative method demonstrations.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity transition or geometry.
No test of capacity competition or dedicated dimensions.
No test of alternative causes of polysemanticity.
Does not measure distribution of features across neurons, or SAE recovery of model features beyond supervised task separability.
Does not test SAE feature completeness, canonicality, or stability across SAEs or models. The Neuronpedia labels in Tables 2 and 5–9 include many off-task features, but this is not analysed.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T3' and its V4 'supports' label are not justified. The representation analyses are qualitative, supervised, method-motivating figures without numbers or uncertainty. The SAE size cited for Fig 3a (16K) conflicts with the LLaMA SAE size (32K), so the subject of R3 and R4 is unclear. The steering tables were correctly excluded.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions, their overlap geometry, or a sparsity-dependent transition.
Does not test whether polysemanticity arises from capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.

The analyses concern task-class separability and selected SAE dimensions in specified LLM tasks; they do not establish that SAEs recover all underlying model features or that features are spread across neurons.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable canonical units of model representation.
Does not test whether model features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: LLaMA3.1-8b
rows.operation_detail: Compared class-wise activation patterns in raw residual space and SAE-encoded space.
rows.baseline: Raw residual-space activations are described as distributed without clear class-specific structure.
rows.value: The SAE space shows several dimensions with strong and consistent differences between classes.
rows.note: The paper describes a comparison of heatmaps and states that sentiment patterns are more concentrated and high-contrast in SAE space.
rows.check: Qualitative heatmap of the top supervised class-discriminative dimensions (text says top 20, the figure shows top 30). Higher class contrast in SAE space than in raw residual space reflects the selection procedure and steering utility. It is not a measure of features being spread across neurons or of SAE recovery of model features. No numbers are given.

rows.subject: LLaMA3.1-8b
rows.operation_detail: Compared class-wise activation patterns in raw residual space and SAE-encoded space.
rows.baseline: Raw residual-space activations are described as distributed without clear class-specific structure.
rows.value: The SAE space shows several dimensions with strong and consistent differences between classes; truthfulness patterns are described as relatively more distributed than sentiment patterns.
rows.note: The paper reports class-discriminative SAE patterns, while noting that truthfulness patterns are less concentrated than sentiment patterns.
rows.check: Same issue as R1, for truthfulness. This is a qualitative separability comparison motivating the method, not a test of V4.

rows.subject: LLaMA3.1-8b
rows.operation_detail: Measured consistency of the selected top-128 SAE dimensions across ensembles of linear classifiers trained on random data subsets.
rows.value: The selected top-128 dimensions remain perfectly consistent across ensemble sizes M = 1 to M = 50; the coefficient of variation of importance scores decreases as M increases.
rows.note: This is stability of task-selected dimensions across classifier ensembles, not evidence of canonical feature stability across models or contexts.
rows.check: This is the stability of the study's own F-statistic and probe dimension selection across M classifiers on data subsets, i.e. a selection value for its method. The subject is unclear: the text says a 16K SAE space, but LLaMA3.1-8B used a 32K SAE, so the model may be Gemma, not LLaMA. It does not bear on any version.

rows.subject: LLaMA3.1-8b
rows.operation_detail: Incrementally measured class separability using top-ranked dimensions from the selected SAE subspace.
rows.measure: Difference between mean projection scores for positive and negative samples
rows.value: A small number of the highest-ranked dimensions gives substantial class separation, with diminishing returns as additional dimensions are included.
rows.note: The paper describes the trend but does not state exact plotted values in the text.
rows.check: This is the separation score used to choose d_steer in the method, a method-internal selection curve. The subject model is not stated in the text. No values are given.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: LLaMA3.1-8b, layer 16, sentiment and truthfulness analyses
reader_labels.reason: The SAE representations show class-discriminative activation patterns, stable selected dimensions, and separability from a small subset of dimensions (R1–R4).
